q-129382.name: Question 1
q-129382.problem: Calculate $\text{Var}[\frac{p}{q}],$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants and $q\ne 0.$
q-129382.worked_solution:
Recall that for any constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[a]=0.
$$

Therefore, since $p$ and $q$ are constants and $q\ne 0,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\frac{p}{q}]=0.
$$

q-109076.name: Question 7
q-109076.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

$$

q-109070.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{9}{2},$ calculate $\text{Var}[\frac{1}{2}X].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $3$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{5}{8}$ |
q-109070.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{2}X] & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{9}{2}.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6) \\  & =9\cdot \frac{1}{4}+36\cdot \frac{5}{8} \\  & =\frac{99}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{99}{4}-{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{2}X] & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-5X] & =(-5)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}\end{aligned}

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{9}^{2}\cdot f(9) \\  & =25(\frac{1}{5})+36(\frac{2}{5})+81(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{259}{5}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-5X] & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \frac{14}{5} \\  & =14\cdot 5 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{5}-4X] & ={(-4)}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =16\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{3}{8})+1(\frac{1}{2})+4(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =1-{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{5}-4X] & =16\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =16\cdot \frac{7}{16} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
